title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos of prominent Dutch women, created by placing their faces onto explicit content, were distributed on a platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos targeted artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. The system created financial incentives for creators to produce these videos and allowed them to remain anonymous while profiting from views.

This is a failure of platform moderation at deployment. The system enabled the creation and distribution of non-consensual intimate imagery without detecting or blocking it, despite such content being illegal under Dutch revenge porn laws. It would have required either automated detection of deepfake pornography before distribution, human review of flagged content, or robust age verification and content filtering before content reached users.

It is not established how long the videos remained on the platform, whether the platform was aware of them before complaints, or what specific enforcement actions resulted from victims' reports to police and prosecutors.

summary:
Several prominent Dutch women are considering legal action after finding themselves in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The videos feature Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. The interim Justice Minister called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed to NOS that they have filed complaints or are considering legal action.

Deepfake pornography, where a person's face is digitally placed onto explicit content, falls under revenge porn laws and is punishable in the Netherlands. Creators are incentivized financially based on video views and are advised to remain anonymous on the platform. Legal experts recommend victims file police reports, which could lead to the Public Prosecutor attempting to shut down the website. Other options include starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with the data protection authority, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued action against a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort, who received a conditional 180-hour community service sentence in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
